name: Sympathetic trunk and ganglia
summary: A chain of ganglia running along each side of the vertebral column from the skull base to the coccyx, receiving preganglionic fibers from the T1–L2 segments through white rami communicantes and distributing postganglionic fibers to every spinal nerve through gray rami, to the head along the carotid arteries and to the viscera through cardiac, pulmonary and splanchnic nerves. Its three cervical ganglia (superior, middle and stellate) carry the entire sympathetic supply of the head and neck, so lesions of the chain in the neck or chest apex (Pancoast tumor, carotid dissection, surgery) cause Horner syndrome.

anatomy.location: Paravertebral gutter on each side from C1 to the coccyx: cervical ganglia in front of the transverse processes behind the carotid sheath, thoracic ganglia on the heads of the ribs, lumbar ganglia on the vertebral bodies, sacral ganglia medial to the anterior sacral foramina, joining at the ganglion impar.

subdivisions.name: Superior cervical ganglion
subdivisions.note: C1–C4 level; postganglionic fibers to the head (pupil, lid, face sweating) via the internal carotid plexus

subdivisions.name: Thoracic ganglia
subdivisions.note: cardiac and pulmonary nerves; greater, lesser and least splanchnic nerves to the abdomen

function: Distribution of sympathetic outflow: vasoconstriction, sweating, piloerection, pupil dilation, cardiac acceleration, bronchodilation and inhibition of gut motility; adrenal medullary stimulation.

bestView.label: upper cervical region; the chain lies in the paravertebral gutter outside the brain volume

imaging.normalAppearance: Not seen as a discrete structure on routine imaging; the stellate ganglion region at the lung apex and the cervical chain behind the carotid sheath are evaluated on chest CT or neck MRI when a Horner syndrome is being explained.

pathology.finding: Apical lung mass invading the stellate ganglion and lower brachial plexus: Horner syndrome with C8–T1 pain and hand weakness.
Mural hematoma of the internal carotid with a partial Horner syndrome from the sympathetic plexus on the artery.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Chest CT for the apex; neck MRI/MRA for the carotid

lesionEffects.mechanism: Preganglionic (second-order) fibers in the chain or stellate ganglion, or postganglionic fibers along the carotid
Loss of vasoconstrictor and sudomotor supply

lesionEffects.deficit: Loss of the adrenal and cardiac response to stress

examination: Pupil asymmetry in light and dark, ptosis, facial sweating
Skin temperature and sweat pattern of the limbs
Pharmacological pupil testing (apraclonidine, hydroxyamphetamine) to grade the lesion
pearls: Horner syndrome with anhidrosis of the whole face is preganglionic (chain); without anhidrosis it is postganglionic (carotid)
A new Horner syndrome with hand pain: image the lung apex
